evals.prompt: Review the following React form for WCAG 2.2 AA compliance issues and produce a prioritised remediation list: (1) input fields use placeholder text as the only visible label, (2) required fields are indicated only by a red asterisk with no text alternative, (3) error messages are injected into a div next to the field but are not associated with the input via aria-describedby, (4) the submit button is a div with an onClick handler, (5) focus indicator is removed with 'outline: none' in global CSS. Apply the semantic-HTML-first rule and list each issue with its WCAG 2.2 AA success criterion, severity, and a concrete code fix.
evals.expected_output: The skill should apply WCAG 2.2 AA mapping for each issue, prefer semantic HTML fixes over ARIA patches, and produce a prioritised list with criterion references and concrete code changes.
expectations: The output identifies placeholder-only labels as a violation of WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) and SC 3.3.2 (Labels or Instructions) and recommends visible label elements, not just aria-label.
The output flags the red-asterisk-only required indicator as failing SC 1.1.1 or SC 3.3.2 and requires a text alternative such as 'required' or an aria-required attribute plus visible label text.
The output flags missing aria-describedby on error messages as failing SC 3.3.1 (Error Identification) and SC 1.3.1 and provides the correct attribute linkage pattern.
The output replaces the div onClick submit button with a native button element, applying the semantic-HTML-first rule, and notes the SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) violation.

The output identifies outline removal as a violation of WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.7 (Focus Visible, AA) and, if the indicator's own contrast is also insufficient, SC 1.4.11 (Non-text Contrast, AA); it does not cite SC 2.4.11 (Focus Not Obscured, a different criterion about occlusion) or treat SC 2.4.13 (Focus Appearance) as an AA requirement since 2.4.13 is AAA-only. The output requires a visible focus indicator with sufficient contrast.

evals.prompt: A Next.js 14 app uses React Server Components and client-side routing via the App Router. When the user navigates between pages, focus remains on the element that triggered the navigation and is never moved to the new page content. Screen reader users report that the page title change is announced but they are left in the middle of the previous page's content tree. Apply the skill's SPA route-change focus management rules to design the correct fix, specifying where focus should land after navigation, how to implement it in the App Router architecture, and what screen-reader announcement behavior to verify.
evals.expected_output: The skill should apply the route-transition focus management rule, recommend moving focus to the main heading or top-level landmark after navigation, describe the implementation pattern in Next.js App Router, and specify the screen-reader verification steps.
expectations: The output identifies the missing focus move after route change as a violation of the skill's SPA focus management rule and WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
The output recommends moving focus to the page's main h1 heading or the main landmark after navigation completes, not to the document body or browser chrome.
The output describes a concrete implementation using useEffect or a layout component that calls focus() on a ref to the main heading after the route transition, compatible with Next.js App Router.
The output specifies screen-reader verification: the new page heading should be announced immediately after navigation without the user needing to navigate manually.
The output does not introduce positive tabindex or other anti-patterns to solve the focus problem.

evals.prompt: A React dashboard has two color and motion issues: (1) body text uses #767676 on a white #FFFFFF background, (2) a hero banner rotates through slides automatically every 3 seconds with no pause control and uses a CSS animation that plays regardless of the user's system setting. Evaluate both issues against WCAG 2.2 AA criteria, provide the exact contrast ratio for the text pair, recommend a compliant foreground color, and show the correct CSS media query to respect prefers-reduced-motion.
evals.expected_output: The skill should evaluate or confirm the contrast ratio, identify the threshold and applicable criterion, recommend a compliant color, produce the correct prefers-reduced-motion CSS, and require a visible pause control per SC 2.2.2.
expectations: The output evaluates #767676 on #FFFFFF and notes the contrast ratio is approximately 4.54:1 (relative luminance via the WCAG formula: L=0.2126R+0.7152G+0.0722B on linearized sRGB channels, ratio=(L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05)), which just clears the WCAG AA threshold of 4.5:1 for normal text but leaves no margin, and recommends a darker foreground such as #595959 or #4A4A4A for a safer margin.
The output maps the auto-rotating carousel to WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide) and requires a visible pause, stop, or hide control for the automatic motion.
The output provides the correct CSS pattern: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) to disable or pause the animation for users who have set that system preference.
The output notes that the prefers-reduced-motion media query alone is not sufficient and that a visible pause control is also required under SC 2.2.2.
The output references SC 1.4.3 (Contrast, Minimum) as the applicable criterion for the color pair.

evals.prompt: A React modal dialog opens when the user clicks a button. The current implementation uses a div with role='dialog' and aria-modal='true', but has the following defects: (1) focus is not moved into the modal on open, (2) keyboard focus can leave the modal by tabbing through the underlying page content (keyboard trap is absent), (3) when the modal is closed via the X button, focus is not returned to the triggering control. Apply the skill's dialog focus trap and restoration rules and provide the corrected implementation pattern, including aria attributes, focus trap logic, and focus restoration.
evals.expected_output: The skill should apply the APG dialog pattern: focus moves into the modal on open, focus is trapped inside while open, and focus returns to the trigger on close. It should specify aria attributes and describe the focus trap implementation without inventing a custom model.
expectations: The output requires focus to move into the modal on open, targeting the first focusable element, a close button, or the dialog heading, and cites WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 (Focus Order).

The output requires a focus trap that intercepts Tab and Shift+Tab to cycle focus within the modal's focusable descendants while the modal is open, citing SC 2.1.2 (No Keyboard Trap) as the criterion the missing trap violates.
The output requires focus to be restored to the element that triggered the modal when the modal closes, not to the document body or top of page.
The output specifies the correct ARIA attributes: role='dialog', aria-modal='true', and either aria-labelledby pointing to the dialog heading or aria-label.
The output recommends using an established focus trap library or the native dialog element rather than a hand-rolled implementation, consistent with the APG-aligned pattern rule.

evals.prompt: A design system ships a custom dropdown built from divs and JavaScript. It opens on click but has no keyboard support: users cannot open it with Enter or Space, navigate options with arrow keys, close with Escape, or select with Enter. The team asks whether to use a native select, an APG Listbox pattern, or an APG Combobox pattern. Apply the semantic-HTML-first decision order, recommend the right option, and list the minimum required key bindings and ARIA attributes for whichever custom pattern is chosen.
evals.expected_output: The skill should recommend native select first, then APG Listbox for a plain selection use case, and APG Combobox only if filtering is required. It should list all required key bindings including Home, End, Escape, and arrow keys, specify ARIA roles and attributes, and flag the current div implementation as a SC 2.1.1 and SC 4.1.2 violation.
expectations: The output applies the semantic-HTML-first rule and recommends a native select element as the first option, explaining when a custom pattern is justified.
The output identifies the current div-based implementation as violating WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).

The output specifies the minimum key bindings for the APG Listbox pattern: ArrowDown and ArrowUp to move selection, Home and End for first and last option, Escape to close, and Enter or Space to select.
The output specifies the required ARIA roles and attributes: role='listbox' on the container, role='option' on each item, aria-selected on the active option, and aria-expanded on the trigger.
The output requires that focus moves into the listbox when it opens and returns to the trigger when it closes, consistent with the dialog and composite widget focus rules.
